title: Evaluation of the canonical Künneth–Verdier map
statement:
Fix the global finite-field and coefficient conventions of
[def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$,
$s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $A=A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$.
Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, $a_Y:Y\to s$ their second
structure map, and $p_X,p_Y$ the projections of $Z=X\times_kY$.
Assume $a_Y$ and $p_X$ are exceptionally admissible at $A$
[def-trf-admissibility]. Let $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and
$N\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$, using [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].
Use the geometric derived pullback, tensor and internal Hom of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Put
$\omega_Y=Ra_Y^!A_s$, $D_YN=R\mathcal Hom_A(N,\omega_Y)$ and let
$\operatorname{ev}_N:D_YN\otimes_A^LN\to\omega_Y$ be the evaluation of
[def-trf-dualizing-complex]. Write
$B=M\boxtimes_A^LD_YN$, $U=Lp_Y^*N$ and
$T=M\boxtimes_A^L\omega_Y$, with external products as in
[def-trf-external-product]. Let
$\alpha:T\to Rp_X^!M$ and
$\kappa_{M,N}:B\to R\mathcal Hom_A(U,Rp_X^!M)$ be the specified maps
of [def-sf-kv-maps] (ii), (iv). Define $e:B\otimes_A^LU\to T$ by
$$
B\otimes_A^LU
\xrightarrow{\rho}
Lp_X^*M\otimes_A^LLp_Y^*(D_YN\otimes_A^LN)
\xrightarrow{1\otimes Lp_Y^*\operatorname{ev}_N}T,
$$
where $\rho$ is tensor reassociation followed by the inverse of the
natural pullback–tensor comparison of
[lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. All constraints use
the signed derived tensor structure specified in [def-sf-kv-maps] (iii).
Then the tensor–Hom transpose of $\kappa_{M,N}$ is $\alpha\circ e$;
equivalently, with $\operatorname{ev}_{U,Rp_X^!M}$ the internal-Hom
evaluation,
$$
\operatorname{ev}_{U,Rp_X^!M}\circ(\kappa_{M,N}\otimes1_U)
=\alpha\circ e.
$$
This equality is natural in $M$ and $N$ on these domains.

source.place: thm-trf-verdier-duality proof Step 3, evaluation compatibility; product-map definition (iii)–(iv), unit specialization and tensor–Hom transpose

proof.text:
Write $H(U,V)=R\mathcal Hom_A(U,V)$ and suppress $\otimes_A^L$ in this proof. Apply the natural internal currying isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] and then [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] to obtain the natural bijection
$$\Phi_{P,U,V}:\operatorname{Hom}(P,H(U,V))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(P\otimes U,V).$$
Define $\operatorname{ev}_{U,V}=\Phi_{H(U,V),U,V}(1)$. Naturality in $P$, applied to $f:P\to H(U,V)$ and the identity of $H(U,V)$, gives $\Phi(f)=\operatorname{ev}_{U,V}\circ(f\otimes1_U)$. Naturality in $V$ gives, for $a:V\to V'$, $\Phi(H(U,a)\circ f)=a\circ\Phi(f)$. These are direct substitutions in the cited natural isomorphisms; no boundedness, perfectness or invertibility of $a$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 08J9, lemma-internal-hom, and Tag 08JA, lemma-section-RHom-over-U; take global H^0 of currying

proof.text: Let $\beta:B\to H(U,T)$ be the first arrow in clause (iv) of [def-sf-kv-maps]. Its clause (iii) specifies its transpose: reassociate the external product of the two internal Homs tensored with the two inputs, then apply their two evaluations. Substitute $(E_1,L_1)=(A_X,M)$ and $(E_2,L_2)=(N,\omega_Y)$. Under $H(A_X,M)\cong M$, the first evaluation is the unit action $M\otimes A_X\to M$: this unit identification is precisely the transpose of the unit action. The other evaluation is $\operatorname{ev}_N$ by [def-trf-dualizing-complex]. Thus the transpose first identifies $(Lp_X^*M\otimes Lp_Y^*D_YN)\otimes Lp_Y^*N$ with $Lp_X^*M\otimes Lp_Y^*(D_YN\otimes N)$ and then applies $1\otimes Lp_Y^*\operatorname{ev}_N$. This is exactly $e$. The comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] has direction $Lp_Y^*(D_YN\otimes N)\to Lp_Y^*D_YN\otimes Lp_Y^*N$, so this calculation uses its inverse. Compatibility with the unit, associativity and signed symmetry is explicitly supplied by [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. In the two-evaluation shuffle, the only interchange removed on specializing is with $A_X$ in degree zero, hence contributes sign $+1$; $D_YN$ and $N$ retain their order. Consequently $\Phi(\beta)=e$, including the specified signs.

source.place: clauses (iii) and (iv): two evaluations and the coefficient-unit specialization

proof.text:
Put $Q=Rp_X^!M$. Clause (iv) of [def-sf-kv-maps] says $\kappa_{M,N}=H(U,\alpha)\circ\beta$. The postcomposition identity of Step 1 and Step 2 give
$$\Phi(\kappa_{M,N})=\alpha\circ\Phi(\beta)=\alpha\circ e.$$
The evaluation description of $\Phi$ from Step 1 rewrites the left side as $\operatorname{ev}_{U,Q}\circ(\kappa_{M,N}\otimes1_U)$, which proves both formulations of the asserted equality. This uses only the definition of the two arrows and naturality of the adjunction; it assumes neither that $\kappa$ is an isomorphism nor that $N$ is site-perfect.

source.place: clause (iv): composite with RHom(1,alpha) and its tensor–Hom transpose

proof.text: For $v:M\to M'$, write $B(v)=Lp_X^*v\otimes1$, $T(v)=Lp_X^*v\otimes1$ and $Q(v)=Rp_X^!v$. The formula for $e$ gives $e_{M',N}\circ(B(v)\otimes1)=T(v)\circ e_{M,N}$ by tensor functoriality and naturality of the pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The map $\alpha$ is natural in $M$: in clause (ii) of [def-sf-kv-maps] its untransposed map is $(\varepsilon_1\boxtimes\varepsilon_2)\circ\mathrm{Ku}_!$, where $\mathrm{Ku}_!$ is the natural relative-product map of [thm-sf-kunneth-relative] followed by the natural base-change identifications of clause (i). Hence counit naturality and the natural exceptional adjunction give $Q(v)\circ\alpha_M=\alpha_{M'}\circ T(v)$. Therefore $Q(v)\circ\alpha_M\circ e_{M,N}=\alpha_{M'}\circ e_{M',N}\circ(B(v)\otimes1)$. Naturality of $\Phi$ in Step 1 gives the same square for $\kappa$, so the equality in Step 3 is natural in $M$. All these uses are on the finite-Tor domains already stipulated by the product-map definition; its naturality theorem is applied with separated finite-type target base $X\times_k s\cong X$.

source.place: clauses (i), (ii), (iv): natural compact-support product, counits, and their adjunction mates

proof.text:
For $w:N'\to N$, let $D_Yw:D_YN\to D_YN'$ be the internal-Hom action specified in [def-trf-dualizing-complex]. Naturality of the bijection in Step 1 in its second input, applied to an identity internal-Hom map, gives
$$\operatorname{ev}_{N'}\circ(D_Yw\otimes1_{N'})=\operatorname{ev}_{N}\circ(1_{D_YN}\otimes w).$$
Pull back this equality and tensor with $Lp_X^*M$. The natural pullback–tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and the signed constraints of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] yield
$$e_{M,N'}\circ((1\boxtimes D_Yw)\otimes1_{Lp_Y^*N'})=e_{M,N}\circ(1_B\otimes Lp_Y^*w).$$
Both sides have source $(M\boxtimes D_YN)\otimes Lp_Y^*N'$ and target $T$. Postcompose with $\alpha_M$, which is independent of $N$. Transposing by the same natural bijection gives
$$\kappa_{M,N'}\circ(1\boxtimes D_Yw)=H(Lp_Y^*w,1_Q)\circ\kappa_{M,N}.$$
This is the required contravariant naturality in $N$, and the displayed uncurried square shows that the equality of Step 3 respects it. Together with Step 4 it proves naturality on the entire stated domain.

source.place: clauses (iii)–(iv): naturality of the two evaluations in the internal-Hom input
